detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

To avoid main memory OOM when offload, add an opt-in `model.lora.resync_base` flag for LoRA adapter mode (`model.lora.merge=False`). When it is set, the rollout releases the base weights on sleep, and the trainer re-syncs the full base weights before the adapter on every weight update. The refit cost is then similar to `merge=True` (full weights every step), plus the usual adapter load. The flag defaults to `False`, which keeps the current behavior.

- **vLLM**: adapter mode today pins the rollout to level-1 sleep, which offloads the base weights to CPU memory on every sleep and copies them back on wake-up. With `resync_base=True`, a HYBRID rollout eligible for level 2 discards the base and receives it from the actor before the adapter update. A COLOCATED server can wake without an actor upload and keeps level 1.
- **SGLang**: adapter mode today releases only the kv_cache on sleep, so the base weights stay on GPU through training. With `resync_base=True` sleep releases the weights too. HYBRID mode always launches SGLang with `enable_weights_cpu_backup=True`, so on SGLang this frees the GPU memory the base holds during training but still keeps a CPU copy.

PR #7304 addresses the first SGLang resume with adapter weights already resident. This PR adds optional base re-transfer on every update and covers both vLLM and SGLang.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [X] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+resync_base, https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+lora+sleep+level
- [X] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.
  - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching`

### Test

DSW CPU validation passed all 20 tests at `6dc9959d`, including a two-rank Gloo reconstruction of FSDP2 base weights.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' python -m pytest -q \
  tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_mtp_hybrid_sleep_acceptance_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/rollout_sglang/test_lora_merge_mode_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_fsdp2_lora_base_export_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_fsdp_lora_base_export_staging_on_cpu.py -rs
```

All configured pre-commit hooks passed for the three changed files. AI assistance was used for the review follow-up and regression tests.

### API and Usage Example

New config key `model.lora.resync_base` (default `False`). It only has an effect when `model.lora.merge=False`, with `rollout.name=vllm` or `rollout.name=sglang`.

```bash
python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=32 \
    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=False \
    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.resync_base=True \
    ...  # Megatron sets the rank via actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.rank instead
```

### Design & Code Changes

1. `verl/trainer/config/model/hf_model.yaml`: add `lora.resync_base: False` and regenerate the `_generated_ppo_*_trainer.yaml` files. The key is added to the shared model config, so it also appears under `critic.model.lora`, where it is unused.
2. `verl/workers/engine_workers.py`: `ActorRolloutRefWorker` reads `lora.resync_base` at init. In the HYBRID trainer’s `naive` update path, adapter mode runs the base sync on every update when `resync_base=True`. The rollout backend selects its sleep level before the first sleep. The base sync reuses the existing first-sync path (`get_per_tensor_param(base_sync_done=False)`, then `rollout.update_weights(..., base_sync_done=False)`), which previously ran only once, when the rollout started from a `dummy` load format.
3. `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py`: `_resolve_sleep_level()` returns 2 instead of 1 for adapter mode when `lora.resync_base` is set. MTP rollout and NPU are still checked first and keep level 1; with `resync_base` they re-sync the base redundantly but stay correct.
4. `verl/workers/rollout/sglang_rollout/`: add `lora_base_kept_on_sleep()` to `utils.py`, which is true in adapter mode unless `lora.resync_base` is set. `SGLangHttpServer.sleep()`, the COLOCATED branch of `wake_up()`, and the initial `ServerAdapter.sleep_level` use it instead of `lora_served_as_adapter()`, so with `resync_base` the server releases `weights` on sleep and `update_weights` resumes them before the base re-sync. Without this, `update_weights` would resume a `weights` tag that sleep never released, which is the `KeyError: 'weights'` from #7289. `enable_lora` and the per-request `lora_path` still follow `lora_served_as_adapter()`.

Nothing changes unless `resync_base=True`; `merge=True` and full-parameter runs are unaffected.

+import pytest

+from torch.distributed.device_mesh import init_device_mesh
+from torch.distributed.fsdp import fully_shard
+from torch.distributed.tensor import DTensor
+
+from verl.utils.fsdp_utils import collect_lora_params
+
+peft = pytest.importorskip("peft")
+
+
+class _TinyModel(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.proj = torch.nn.Linear(8, 6, bias=False)
+        self.head = torch.nn.Linear(6, 4)
+
+
+def _base_export_worker(rank, world_size, rendezvous_file):
+    dist.init_process_group(
+        backend="gloo",
+        init_method=f"file://{rendezvous_file}",
+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=world_size,
+    )
+    try:
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        model = peft.get_peft_model(_TinyModel(), peft.LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["proj"]))
+        expected = {
+            "proj.weight": model.base_model.model.proj.base_layer.weight.detach().clone(),
+            "head.weight": model.base_model.model.head.weight.detach().clone(),
+            "head.bias": model.base_model.model.head.bias.detach().clone(),
+        }
+        fully_shard(model, mesh=init_device_mesh("cpu", (world_size,)))
+
+        params = collect_lora_params(model, layered_summon=False, base_sync_done=False)
+
+        # Base names only, with the LoRA wrapper stripped and no adapter tensors.
+        assert sorted(params) == sorted(expected)
+        # Still sharded: each rank holds its slice until the caller gathers one tensor at a time.
+        for name, param in params.items():
+            assert isinstance(param, DTensor), name
+            assert param.to_local().numel() < param.numel(), name
+            torch.testing.assert_close(param.full_tensor(), expected[name])
+
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="rollout.layered_summon=True cannot export the LoRA base weights"):
+            collect_lora_params(model, layered_summon=True, base_sync_done=False)
+    finally:
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+def test_fsdp2_lora_base_export_stays_sharded(tmp_path):
+    world_size = 2
+    mp.spawn(
+        _base_export_worker,
+        args=(world_size, str(tmp_path / "fsdp2_rdzv")),
+        nprocs=world_size,
+        join=True,
+    )

Commit 6dc9959d covers the outstanding general review comments about LoRA sleep and resync.

- A vLLM COLOCATED replica can wake and serve without an actor upload. This also applies to a colocated teacher or reward model. Level 1 preserves its weights through that transition. In the HYBRID naive path the actor explicitly uploads the base and then the adapter on each resync, so level 2 is valid there. The new test calls `sleep()` in both modes and checks the direct COLOCATED wake. [review 5490222055](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8032#pullrequestreview-5490222055) · [review 5758402709](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8032#pullrequestreview-5758402709) · [review 5645050286](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8032#pullrequestreview-5645050286)
- The trainer no longer writes `rollout.sleep_level` inside `update_weights()`. SGLang selects the level when its adapter is constructed, before the first sleep or resume. vLLM selects it on the server at sleep time. [review 5491476959](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8032#pullrequestreview-5491476959)
- `update_weights()` checks the effective sync mode, including a per-call override. Active adapter resync raises before a non-naive transfer because it cannot restore the adapter. A forced naive update can perform both uploads. The HYBRID resolver can therefore retain level 2 for supported resyncs; the separate KV-cache-only path preserves adapter weights at level 1. [review 5705209319](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8032#pullrequestreview-5705209319) · [review 5730449288](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8032#pullrequestreview-5730449288)

Validation on DSW with CUDA disabled passed all 20 tests across the vLLM sleep, SGLang adapter policy, FSDP2 base export and FSDP staging suites. The FSDP2 export test used two Gloo ranks. All pre-commit hooks for the changed files passed.
